title: Top-10 Indian Firms Lose Rs 1 Lakh Crore in Market Cap; TCS Takes Biggest Hit
excerpt: Five of India's 10 most-valued companies saw their combined market valuation erode by Rs 1 lakh crore last week, with Tata Consultancy Services leading the decline.
body:
• Five of India's top-10 most valued companies lost a combined Rs 1 lakh crore in market capitalization last week
  • Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) took the biggest hit among the laggards amid broader weakness in IT stocks
  • The remaining five firms in the top-10 pack managed to add to their valuations, partially offsetting the losses

Five of India's 10 most-valued listed companies saw their combined market capitalization erode by approximately Rs 1 lakh crore last week, with Tata Consultancy Services taking the biggest hit as IT stocks came under pressure.

The decline came in a week that saw the broader market trade with a cautious tone. The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty both ended the week lower, reflecting investor wariness amid a mix of global and domestic headwinds.

TCS Leads the Decline

TCS, the country's largest IT services company by market capitalization, was the biggest laggard among the top-10 firms. The stock has been under pressure as investors weigh the outlook for IT services spending against a backdrop of global economic uncertainty and shifting client priorities toward AI-related projects.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=r0Y4-3e8uC4

The IT sector has faced a challenging period as discretionary technology spending by large enterprise clients remains subdued. While TCS reported a 4.61% increase in its June-quarter net profit to Rs 13,349 crore, the company's near-term guidance has been tempered by geopolitical disruptions and slower deal ramp-ups in key markets.

A Split Week for Blue-Chips

The erosion was not uniform across the top-10 pack. While five firms saw their valuations decline, the remaining five managed gains, partially offsetting the overall damage.

The pattern reflects the increasingly bifurcated nature of India's large-cap market, where sector rotation and earnings divergence are driving sharply different outcomes even among the most liquid names.

Banking and financial stocks have traded in a mixed band following a round of quarterly earnings that showed varying margin trajectories across lenders. Consumer-facing companies have grappled with demand moderation, while energy and telecom names have benefited from structural tailwinds.

Market Context

The weekly decline in top-10 valuations is part of a broader trend of volatility that has marked Indian equity markets through much of 2026. After a strong start to the year, the Sensex and Nifty have traded sideways as investors digest a complex mix of factors: elevated crude oil prices, rupee weakness, global interest-rate uncertainty, and uneven corporate earnings.

"Markets witnessed a cautious week with benchmark indices reflecting underlying uncertainty as investors balanced strong domestic fundamentals against global headwinds."

— Market analysts

Reliance Industries has continued to hold the top spot as India's most valued company, followed by other heavyweights across banking, telecom, IT, and financial services.

What to Watch

Market participants will be watching for further cues from the ongoing earnings season, movement in global bond yields, and any shifts in foreign institutional investor (FII) flows. The IT sector's trajectory will be particularly closely tracked, given TCS's outsized influence on both the benchmark indices and overall market-cap rankings.

Weekly market-cap movements among India's top firms have become a closely followed barometer of institutional sentiment, offering a snapshot of where large pools of capital are rotating in a market that now ranks among the world's five largest by total capitalization.
